name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Resonance Hammer RH-3 'Earthquake'
description: A crew-served sonic weapon that generates a focused infrasonic pulse capable of inducing structural resonance in buildings, vehicles, and human bone. The RH-3 projects sound waves between 7-12 Hz at extreme amplitude through a parabolic emitter dish, creating a cone of effect where targets experience violent nausea, loss of equilibrium, and at close range, micro-fractures in the skeletal system. The weapon leaves no visible damage on structures but can fatigue load-bearing elements to the point of collapse over repeated application.
specifications:
frequency range: 7-12 Hz variable
amplitude: 185 dB at source
effective range: 10-80 meters cone
power source: Vehicle-mounted generator or heavy capacitor bank
weight: 62 kg (emitter assembly)
crew: 2 operators minimum
structural fatigue threshold: 4-6 sustained pulses on standard ferrocrete
story_hooks: Buildings in a Tier 2 neighborhood are spontaneously collapsing — structural engineers suspect infrasonic fatigue but no weapon deployments have been reported in the area.
A black market dealer is offering a miniaturized version of the RH-3 emitter that fits in a backpack — if it works, it changes the calculus of urban warfare entirely.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist parabolic dish weapon mounted on a tripod or vehicle frame. The RH-3 resembles a massive satellite receiver crossed with a bass amplifier—all curved geometry and deliberate acoustic engineering. It presents as a weapon of structural violence rather than ballistic elegance.
physical_description.dimensions: Parabolic dish diameter: 120 cm; depth from mount point to emitter focus: 85 cm; tripod spread: 145 cm wide × 160 cm long; total height when mounted: 210 cm. Emitter assembly weighs 62 kg but spans roughly 145 cm at widest points.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty, immobile without equipment. The parabolic dish has mass that demands respect—it requires at least two operators and solid mounting. Not a shoulder-fired weapon; feels anchored, permanent, geological.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium composite for the parabolic dish; reinforced steel subframe and tripod; internal layering of acoustic dampening ceramics and meta-materials to focus infrasonic projection.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with subtle heat-stressed bronze patina on the dish interior from sustained acoustic resonance. Exterior shows weather-resistant polymer coating. Mounting brackets display bare welded steel with minimal finish—functional, not decorative.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary; dark bronze acoustic interior of parabolic dish; charcoal black control interface and junction boxes. Accent: thin Φ-cyan power indicator lines running along the emitter rim.
physical_description.grip_texture: Grip surfaces use textured rubberized composite for operator hand holds on the tripod adjustment wheels. Control panel buttons are raised tactile switches with slight resistance. Cable connections are armored with braided polymer sleeves.
distinctive_features: Massive parabolic dish with visible internal acoustic layering—honeycomb ceramic weave visible at certain angles
Ring of micro-vents around the focal point emitter where infrasonic pulses concentrate
Triangulated tripod with adjustable height and azimuth/elevation control wheels etched with degree markers
Power coupling port on rear frame with heavy-duty connector housing—glowing Φ-cyan status indicator when active
Vibration dampening isolators at all tripod feet—visible as spring-loaded cylindrical assemblies
Serial plate mounted on starboard side of frame: ZHENG-DAO HI | RH-3 EARTHQUAKE | MMXXVI | Military Restricted
Deep linear scoring on the dish surface—evidence of acoustic testing or field use
Faint concentric ring patterns in the finish suggesting frequency calibration marks
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO HEAVY INDUSTRIES logo stamped in sharp sans-serif on the control interface housing. Serial number plate in top-right of rear frame assembly. Small frequency specification placard mounted near the emitter focus point. Manufacturing date stamp (MMXXVI) on the tripod joint.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. The parabolic surface shows micro-abrasions from years of acoustic discharge, with subtle stress discoloration patterns radiating from the focal emitter. Tripod joints are clean and lubricated; mounting hardware shows signs of repeated calibration adjustments. No visible structural damage—this is a weapon that accumulates evidence through subtlety rather than obvious battle scars.
